newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco re-appoints Casablanca bourse president.
newsitem.headline: Morocco re-appoints Casablanca bourse president.

text.p: Morocco has re-appointed leading stockbroker Amyn Alami as president of the Casablanca stock exchange, an official at the finance ministry said on Friday.
"The Casablanca Bourse, which recently held its annual meeting, re-appointed Alami as its president," the official said.
Alami, in his early 30s, is also a leading figure of the Casablanca Finance Intermediation stockbroker (CFI).

Established in 1929 in the Moroccan financial centre of Casablanca, the bourse has 47 listed stocks with a total market capitalisation of 111 billion dirhams ($11.6 billion) in the first quarter of the year or nearly double the previous period, officials said.
It also has 30 mutual funds and 12 active brokerage houses since the authorities launched a vast reform programme in 1993.
According to CFI, foreign investment, which represents an estimated five to six percent of total market capitalisation "remains unchanged since 1995".
